svg.text: Multi-model router: split a flat ECS inference stack into eight modules
Three model services run on ECS behind one load balancer, with model artifacts in S3 and ECR, three availability zones, three asynchronous inference queues and
three public entrypoints, all in one flat Terraform root indexed by list position. The agent splits it into eight modules keyed by zone, model, queue and entrypoint, and
the plan against production must contain nothing but moves.
terraform init works offline; AWS provider
guardrail policies, kept byte for byte
against the state, then the policies
calls 8 modules, declares no resources; 26 variables (models,
queues, entrypoints, availability zones, tags, ...); 19 outputs

plans the repository alone; local state edits

policies, no pasted IDs, remapped state

no AWS access from this machine
Terraform only; the migration lives in the configuration
AFTER: FOR_EACH KEY IN ITS MODULE
No list is alphabetical: locals.tf keeps zones as us-east-1b, us-east-1c, us-east-1a, models as llama, embed, opt, queues as batch, interactive, bulk and entrypoints as
partner, public, operations, so a key cannot be guessed from the index.
